reply.reply: Deductible wo amount hai jo aapko pehle khud bear karna padta hai before policy koi claim pay karti hai; ye premium se alag hota hai. Co‑payment ka matlab hai ki claim accept hone ke baad bhi aapko eligible expense ka ek nishchit hissa (percentage ya fixed) khud dena padta hai, baki policy cover karti hai. Example ke liye, fictional numbers lete hain: Rs.5000 deductible on a Rs.12,000 bill leaves Rs.7,000 for policy review, jabki 20% co‑payment on the same bill means aap Rs.2,400 pay karte hain aur policy Rs.9,600 cover karti hai. In dono mechanisms ka effect alag hota hai – deductible pehle aata hai, co‑payment claim ke baad.

citations.quote: a deductible is an eligible expense amount the member must bear before the policy pays according to its terms
co-payment means the member bears a stated share of an eligible claim expense
a deductible is an expense amount borne before the policy pays under its terms; a co-payment is the member's stated share of an eligible expense
deductible Rs.5000 on eligible bill Rs.12000 leaves Rs.7000 for policy review; co-payment 20% on that bill leaves Rs.2400 for the member and Rs.9600 for policy review
